title: Northern Lights dazzle skies across Cumbria from Brampton to Whitehaven
excerpt: Residents across Cumbria were treated to a spectacular display of the Northern Lights over the weekend as the aurora borealis lit up the night sky.
content:
Residents across Cumbria were treated to a spectacular display of the Northern Lights over the weekend as the aurora borealis lit up the night sky.

Photographs and reports emerged from across the county, with the colourful phenomenon visible in locations stretching from Brampton and Carlisle to west Cumbrian towns including Whitehaven as geomagnetic activity brought the lights further south than usual.

The display saw shades of green, pink and purple shimmer across the sky, with stargazers sharing images on social media after clear conditions provided ideal viewing opportunities.

The Northern Lights are more commonly associated with countries closer to the Arctic Circle, but strong solar activity can occasionally make them visible across the UK.

This weekend's display followed a series of coronal mass ejections from the Sun, which increased geomagnetic activity around Earth and expanded the area from which the aurora could be seen.

The Met Office had forecast an increased chance of auroral sightings between October 10 and 13, particularly across Scotland and northern parts of the UK.

Reports of sightings were received across northern England, Scotland and even parts of the Midlands.

According to the weather service, the phenomenon occurs when charged particles from the Sun interact with Earth's magnetic field before colliding with oxygen and nitrogen high in the atmosphere, producing the familiar colourful glow.

Green is the most common colour, while red, purple and blue shades can also be visible depending on the altitude and atmospheric conditions.

Forecasters said there could be further opportunities to spot the Northern Lights over the coming days if skies remain clear, with northern England among the areas that may continue to have a chance of seeing the display.

For many Cumbrians, however, the weekend's spectacle provided one of the most striking celestial displays seen in the county this year, transforming skies from Brampton to Whitehaven into a canvas of colour.
